name: JPYSC
oneLiner: JPYSC is Shinsei Trust & Banking's Ethereum-issued, closed-loop yen stablecoin for verified SBI VC Trade users; external-wallet withdrawals remain disabled.
collateral: Segregated Shinsei Trust & Banking trust accounts holding yen cash and Japanese government bonds, with JGBs capped at 50% of reserves under Japan's Type III Electronic Payment Instrument framework
pegMechanism: Trust-bank-backed JPY stablecoin issued by Shinsei Trust & Banking and distributed by SBI VC Trade. The June 24, 2026 launch is closed-loop for verified SBI VC Trade users; the Ethereum token is deployed, but external-wallet withdrawals and open public-chain circulation remain disabled pending legal and tax policy.

blacklistabilityReview.evidence: At Ethereum block 25712112, the official JPYSC proxy resolved to verified StablecoinV1 implementation 0xba161409749ae95e9bbc1cf3a2dd3fe3e0af1d5e and paused() was false. Verified source gives the current blacklister 0xba1fb3b95cdea5c62dc7c83a9ac8c704160d2356 address-level blacklist/unblacklist power, the pauser 0xf30a72ba1fb9de61a1531fd8a691d046d425ae32 global pause power, and the seizer 0x90de37a09222f08ead6de034aa84dfcddf9ca560 court-order forced-transfer power after an address is blacklisted. Holder transfers enforce both the pause and blacklist gates.

mintAuthority.summary: JPYSC uses renewable per-minter allowances plus a per-minter destination whitelist. No minter was active at the observation block, but an EOA minter admin can immediately authorize a new allowance and the 3-of-4 owner Safe can rotate both operational gates; UUPS upgrades are separated behind a two-day timelock controlled by another 3-of-4 Safe.

controls.label: JPYSC minter administrator
controls.capDescription: The minter administrator can configure or renew a per-minter allowance once the current allowance is zero; the verified implementation imposes no global issuance ceiling.
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25712112, minterAdmin() returned this EOA. Verified source makes configureMinter/removeMinter exclusive to that address and allows any new allowance after the current allowance reaches zero. Complete MinterConfigured/MinterRemoved replay found the two historical operator addresses 0x7e7b8b835b5face8db66ddc28fae589ee7abb647 and 0x03c1dcfbf5aaa334c3a270a5a2b782bcbf1be5fa both removed; direct isMinter and minterAllowance reads returned false and zero for each.

controls.label: JPYSC mint-destination whitelist manager
controls.evidence: whitelistManager() returned this EOA at Ethereum block 25712112. Verified source requires each mint destination to be whitelisted for the calling minter, so this is an independent operational gate but cannot create supply or grant a mint allowance.

controls.label: JPYSC owner and operational-role recovery Safe
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25712112, owner() returned this 3-of-4 Safe. Safe Transaction Service reported version 1.4.1, four owners, no modules, and zero guard. Verified StablecoinV1 lets the owner rotate the minter administrator and mint-destination whitelist manager immediately, so the Safe can authorize a new mint path even though it is deliberately separated from UUPS upgrade authority.

controls.label: JPYSC two-day UUPS upgrade timelock
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25712112, upgradeAuthority() returned this verified TimelockController and getMinDelay() returned 172800 seconds. StablecoinV1 restricts both _authorizeUpgrade and updateUpgradeAuthority to the current upgrade authority, so the token owner cannot bypass the timelock's two-day delay.

controls.label: JPYSC upgrade-governance Safe (timelock proposer/canceller)
controls.evidence: At Ethereum block 25712112, this Safe was 3-of-4, version 1.4.1, with no modules and zero guard. Timelock hasRole checks returned true for its PROPOSER_ROLE and CANCELLER_ROLE; EXECUTOR_ROLE was open to address zero, so anyone may execute a ready operation but only reviewed proposers can schedule one.

sources.label: SBI Shinsei Trust Bank JPYSC terms
SBI Shinsei Trust statutory JPYSC issuance and deposit balances

review.evidence: At Ethereum block 25712112, direct role reads and a complete MinterConfigured/MinterRemoved replay established no live minter but a live EOA minter administrator able to issue renewable allowances without a global on-chain cap. Minting also requires a separately managed per-minter destination whitelist. The 3-of-4 owner Safe can rotate both operational roles; UUPS authority is separated behind a 172800-second TimelockController whose sole live proposer is another 3-of-4 Safe. Official terms state that issuance has no upper limit, so economic cap semantics are unbounded. The only public reserve snapshot retrieved is dated 2026-06-30 and the terms disclaim an issuance audit, so no reconciliation cadence is asserted. SBI Shinsei Trust Bank appears on the FSA's licensed trust-bank list and issues JPYSC as the trust-bank instrument described in official product materials, supporting prudential supervision.

reserves.name: Yen demand deposits in segregated SBI Shinsei Trust Bank trust accounts
reserves.issuerOrObligor: SBI Shinsei Trust & Banking (trustee); underlying deposit banks undisclosed

reserveReview.rationale: R02 refresh 2026-08-08: The trustee's statutory disclosure as of 2026-06-30 showed deposit balances (¥10,008,304,794) at or slightly above the issued amount (¥10,008,294,794) with no JGB line item, i.e. effectively 100% yen demand deposits at that date. The amended PSA trust-type framework (in force since 13 June 2026) permits the issuer to hold up to 50% of trust assets in short-term JGBs/USTs with remaining maturity of 3 months or less or in principal-protected time deposits, with top-up obligations. The issuer's launch release says a portion is planned to be invested in JGBs, but no subsequent cash/JGB percentage split, reserve report, or third-party attestation has been published, and the statutory disclosure page remains unreachable outside Japan. The single bank-deposit slice is therefore retained as the last observed composition, with the 50% cap noted as a structural upper bound rather than an actual allocation.
reserveReview.compositionBasis: Trustee statutory issuance/deposit-balance disclosure dated 2026-06-30; issuer launch release; CoinPost trust-structure explainer; FSA framework rules and Fystack summary bounding permissible JGB allocation.
reserveReview.knownUnknownExposure: Supply has roughly doubled (to about ¥20.6B) since the last retrievable composition disclosure, and the issuer may shift up to 50% of reserves into short-term JGBs/USTs without granular public disclosure; there is no independent attestation program, only trustee statutory disclosure under FSA supervision.

notices.title: Walled-garden circulation; peg-derived price
notices.message: JPYSC circulates only inside verified SBI VC Trade accounts — no external-wallet withdrawals and no public-chain secondary market yet. There are zero trading venues, so the tracked price is peg-derived (¥1.00) rather than market-discovered and cannot reflect market stress; supply and market cap come from the DefiLlama path, as CoinGecko's circulating-supply field is inconsistent with its own market cap. Startale says public-chain circulation is technically ready but awaiting legal and tax clarity.

featuredContent.title: Startale Group and SBI Holdings Introduce JPYSC, the First Trust Bank-Backed JPY Stablecoin
featuredContent.description: JPYSC is a Type III electronic payment instrument issued by Shinsei Trust & Banking, jointly developed with SBI Holdings, distributed via SBI VC Trade, and built for institutional cross-border and treasury payments.

featuredContent.title: SBI Holdings unveils trust bank-backed JPY stablecoin with Q2 launch target
featuredContent.description: JPYSC will be Japan's first trust bank-issued yen stablecoin, distinguishing it from JPYC's prepaid payment instrument classification. Trust-based issuers may allocate up to 50% of reserves to government bonds.

featuredContent.title: SBI and Startale Launch JPYSC, Japan's First Trust-Backed Yen Stablecoin
featuredContent.description: JPYSC goes live June 24 2026 in a closed-loop phase for SBI VC Trade users; the trust-beneficiary structure exempts it from the ¥1M transfer cap and allows up to 50% JGB reserves.

milestones.title: Startale and SBI unveil Strium L1 for tokenized securities and RWA trading
milestones.description: Strium described as destination for a 'complementary currency stack' of JPYSC and USDSC; likely deployment target for JPYSC.

milestones.title: Startale Group and SBI Holdings unveil JPYSC, first trust bank-backed JPY stablecoin
milestones.description: Brand and logo announced; issuer Shinsei Trust & Banking, distributor SBI VC Trade, technical lead Startale Group; Q2 2026 launch target under Japan's Type III electronic payment instrument framework.

milestones.title: Startale closes $63M Series A (SBI $50M + Sony $13M) earmarked for JPYSC expansion
milestones.description: Funds target Strium scaling, stablecoin expansion (JPYSC + USDSC), and Startale App enhancement; confirms JPYSC remains a 2026 priority.

milestones.title: SBI VC Trade begins RLUSD distribution in Japan — JPYSC distributor infrastructure now live
milestones.description: SBI VC Trade, JPYSC's designated distributor, operationally distributing Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin, de-risking the JPYSC distribution pathway.

milestones.title: Japan FSA activates rules for foreign stablecoins as electronic payment instruments
milestones.description: Japan's regulated framework for qualified foreign stablecoins took effect, advancing the regime JPYSC will launch under.

milestones.title: JPYSC goes live (closed-loop) — issued by Shinsei Trust & Banking, distributed via SBI VC Trade
milestones.description: Japan's first trust-bank-backed yen stablecoin launches with first issuance the same day; ~$63M of cash plus up to 50% JGB reserves held in segregated trust accounts under the Type III electronic payment instrument framework. Initial phase is closed-loop — SBI VC Trade account holders only, with no external-wallet withdrawals or public-chain circulation yet.

milestones.title: SBI, DigiFT, and Startale partner on JPYSC-powered settlement for tokenized capital markets
milestones.description: Partnership covers JPYSC-powered settlement and on-chain dividend distribution for tokenized capital-markets products.

milestones.title: SBI VC Trade opens applications for JPYSC Lending, Japan's first trust-based yen stablecoin lending service
milestones.description: Applications opened July 16 2026 with the lending period starting July 23; a promotional 3% annualized yield applies over a 12-week term, with standard yields projected at 1-3% thereafter. The service runs inside the SBI VC Trade account environment and does not change JPYSC's closed-loop status.
